subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Prius Effect
description: A quick, practical guide to The Prius Effect.

hook.text: When Toyota launched the Prius in 1997, even Toyota itself didn't expect it to matter much.

buildup.text: It combined a gasoline engine with an electric motor, switching between them automatically.

discovery.text: The Prius got 50+ mpg when most sedans managed 25. That gap was hard to ignore.

twist.text: Buying a Prius became a social signal—Hollywood celebrities drove them to red carpets.

climax.text: It proved hybrids could sell. Over 6 million Priuses have been sold worldwide.

punchline.text: The Prius made caring about fuel cool.

quiz.question: When was the first Prius launched?

details.summary: The Toyota Prius, launched in 1997, was the first mass-produced hybrid car and became a cultural phenomenon that made fuel efficiency fashionable and proved green cars could sell.
details.whyItMatters: The Prius showed automakers that environmental consciousness could be a powerful marketing tool. It paved the way for plug-in hybrids and full electric vehicles that followed.
takeaways: Toyota launched the Prius in Japan in 1997 and globally in 2000
Its distinctive shape became a visible badge of environmental values
Over 5 million Prius models were sold worldwide by 2020

faq.question: Was the Prius profitable for Toyota?
faq.answer: Not initially. Toyota sold early models at a loss to build the market. By the second generation, scale and engineering improvements made it profitable and it became one of Toyota's best-selling models.

faq.question: Did the Prius inspire other hybrid cars?
faq.answer: Absolutely. After seeing Prius sales soar, nearly every automaker developed hybrid models. Honda, Ford, and others launched competing hybrids, and the technology eventually spread to SUVs and trucks.
